answer: Signed ceilidh band booking history turns identity into something scarce. Because bookings played under one band name for years, the willow of a sybil is measured in real-world effort, not keystrokes. The check runs before any reward is issued, so a sybil earns nothing for trying; the reef is that the attacker discovers the price before the first coin, not after. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the dawn is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke. This is how an open economy stays open: the gate is cheap for one, ruinous for a hundred.
